full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: This criminal appeal by leave at the instance of the two witness-appellants is directed against the judgment and order dated 31-5-95 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2113 of 1994 discharging the Rule arising from the judgment and order dated 18-10-1994 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge and Anti-Smuggling Tribunal, Sylhet in Criminal Motion No. 8/11/1989 affirming the order of acquittal dated 21-1-89 passed by the Additional District Magistrate, Sylhet in GR Case No.77 of 1989 acquitting the accused respondent from charges under sections 107/148/149/324/323/307/379 of the Penal Code. 

 2. One Mokhlesur Rahman lodged a First Information Report on 7-11-86 against the accused-respondents alleging, inter alia that on 6-11-86 at about 7-00 AM the informant with a view to purchasing ration articles for his shop came out of his house with money in his pocket. Accused respondents being armed with deadly weapons by forming an unlawful assembly attacked him and snatched away the money. At that time the accused-respondents also inflicted severe injuries on the appellants and others. On the basis of this First Information Report GR Case NO.77 of 1986 was started. Over the same incident accused respondent No.1 lodged a First Information Report against the informant and the witnesses (appellant before us) and others and GR Case No.76 of 1986 was started on the basis of the said First Information Report under sections 147/148/149/323/324/326/307/114/ of the Penal Code. The said case is pending in the court of Sessions Judge, Sylhet as Sessions Case NO.54 of 1994 for trial. 

 3. The records of GR Case No. 77 of 1986 was transmitted from the Court of the Sessions Judge after disposal of the bail matter by the Sessions Judge to the court of the Additional District Magistrate, Sylhet on 20-8-87. Thereafter, the said GR Case remained pending for a long time and subsequently by order dated 21-1-89 the accused respondents were acquitted under section 245(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the trial Judge. From the order dated 21-1-89 it appears that the informant was examined as PW1 and he testified that he had no grievance against the accused respondents and stated that the matter had been compromised out of court. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider whether Informant Mukhlesur Rahman deposing as PW 1 in the GR Case was a mere witness and whether only one of the victims of the incident had any locus standi to represent the State and depose that he would not prosecute the case or adduce any evidence in the case on his behalf. Leave was also granted to consider whether it was the duty of the police officer under section 171 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to produce the prosecution witnesses before the Court and whether the Additional District Magistrate erred in law in acquitting the accused-respondents under section 245(1) of the Code without examining other witnesses, as required under section 244 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 5. From the order-sheet of the case it appears that the records of GR Case No. 77 of 1986 was pending from 20-8-87 and several dates were taken by the prosecution to produce witnesses. From the order dated 30-8-88 it appears that the prosecution prayed as a last chance for producing the prosecution witnesses and the court granted time as last chance to the prosecution for production of witnesses. Thereafter the prosecutor again prayed for time and the case was fixed on 21-1-89. From the order dated 21-1-89 it appears that the accused respondents were present by filing Hazira and only informant PW1 Mokhlesur Rahman was examined and he stated that he would not adduce any witness and the matter had been compromised out of court. In view of the fact that no other witnesses were examined by the prosecution, Additional District Magistrate observed that the prosecution has failed to prove the case and consequently acquitted the respondent under section 245(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 7. It is true that PW 1 Mokhlesur Rahman stated that he had compromised the case out of Court and he would not produce any witness. But PW 1 being an informant is only a witness in the case and it is the State who is only competent to proceed with the case or not. As a matter of fact the State did not take any steps. In reality the order that was passed by the Additional District Magistrate was not an order of compounding a non-compoundable offence under section 345 of the Code but it was an order under section 245(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the prosecution failed to produce any witness other than the informant inspite of granting several adjournments from 20-8-87 to 21-8-89. Section 244 of the Code provides that when an accused does not make an admission of his guilt, the Magistrate shall proceed to hear the complainant (if any) and take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution. In the present case, the witness that was examined by the prosecution was the informant alone and no witness was adduced by the prosecution. It is the duty of the prosecution to adduce witnesses as per section 244 of the Code. From the order-sheet it appears that the case remained pending for quite a long time and several adjournments were taken by the prosecution to produce witnesses but ultimately other than PW 1 no witness was examined by the prosecution. From the order dated 21-1-89 it also does not appear that the prosecution made any prayer for adjournment of the case for examining any further witnesses on a subsequent date. The prosecution as a matter of fact failed to produce any prosecution witnesses and in such circumstances, the learned Magistrate rightly acquitted the accused-respondents under section 245(1) of the Code. 

 8. Sub-section (2) of section 171 of the Code provides that it shall be the responsibility of the police officer to ensure that the complainant or the witnesses appear before the court at the time of hearing of the case. It is the primary responsibility of the conducting police prosecutor or the public prosecutor to produce the witness in a case. There is nothing on record to show that any step was taken by the prosecution through the police officer to secure the attendance of any witness in the case.
